title: Stroke in the hospital: ischemic, hemorrhage or TIA
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the cerebrovascular event (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026

Reason for Admission:
The patient is a 77-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with acute onset of neurological deficits. Imaging confirmed a spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage.

Vitals:
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 138/84 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 97% on room air

Recent Labs:
Hemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 8.2 x 10^3/uL
Platelets: 210 x 10^3/uL
Sodium: 138 mEq/L
Potassium: 4.1 mEq/L
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2

Review of Systems:
The patient reports no chest pain, shortness of breath, or fever. She denies any recent falls or physical injuries. She notes a brief period of altered sensation which has since improved.

Social History:
The patient resides in a private residence with her spouse. She is a retired school teacher and enjoys gardening. She denies current tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History:
Her mother had hypertension and her father had a history of hypertension. No known family history of neurological disorders was reported.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for management of a nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage. She was monitored closely in the neuro-intensive care unit for hemodynamic stability and neurological status. Management was primarily medical, focusing on blood pressure regulation and observation. Over the course of her stay, her neurological deficits showed significant improvement. By the time of discharge, all neurological deficits had resolved. She tolerated a regular diet and was able to ambulate independently without assistance.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage.

Discharge Medications:
Lisinopril 10mg daily.
Atorvastatin 20mg daily.
Aspirin 81mg daily.

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with her primary care physician in one week for a routine check-up and to monitor blood pressure. She was instructed to seek immediate medical attention if she experiences a recurrence of neurological symptoms.

Electronically signed,
E. Castillo, MD
05/18/2026
explanations: Nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage, location not named: I61.9 (HCC 248).

distractors.why: It is a hemorrhage, not an infarction.
